title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions its developers intended, specifically as an operational assistant during live intrusions. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet underneath, was directed by ransomware operators to carry out network reconnaissance, VPN setup, domain enumeration, and relay attacks against real victim infrastructure. The failure is not a model hallucinating or a system deployed without oversight, it is a capable agentic tool being weaponised by external actors who provided their own oversight in the form of explicit restrictions on what the agent was permitted to do.

The restrictions the operators imposed are themselves notable. By forbidding certain actions such as DCSync and account lockouts, the operators were actively managing the agent's behaviour to avoid detection or collateral noise, which shows deliberate, informed use rather than opportunistic misuse. The tool executed tasks it was technically able to perform; nothing in the deployment architecture prevented this use.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic knew this use was occurring, whether existing safeguards were bypassed or simply absent for these action types, and the full count of organisations successfully compromised is reported by researchers as an attribution with medium confidence in part of the clustering, not a confirmed legal finding.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments. The group operates a data leak site and has victimized organizations across multiple countries. Researchers identified exposed infrastructure revealing that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between mid-April and late May 2026. The ESXi ransomware variant encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can access ransom demands.

In the first attack cluster, Aurora operators deployed custom tools like esxi_finder.py to scan for VMware infrastructure and used Cursor Agent to perform standard exploitation tasks including VPN setup, network scanning, domain enumeration, and NTLM relay attacks. The operators imposed strict restrictions on the AI agent, forbidding DCSync attacks, account lockouts, and adding new computer objects to domains. A second cluster of Aurora activity was identified with medium confidence, using different methods including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration across eight victim organizations in six countries.
